title: Completed normalization and associated graded model of a quadratic local ring
statement:
Let $k$ be a field, and let $(A,\mathfrak m,F)$ be a reduced local $k$-algebra (a ring with a unique maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$, residue field $F=A/\mathfrak m$, and no nonzero nilpotents). Assume that $A$ is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], essentially of finite type over $k$ [def-weil-pbc-essentially-finite-type-algebra], and of Krull dimension one [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. Put $R=\widehat A$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. Suppose given a $k$-algebra section $F\to R$ of the residue map and a residue-preserving continuous $F$-algebra presentation
$$R\cong F[[X,Y]]/(q),\qquad q=aX^2+bXY+cY^2,\qquad b^2-4ac\ne0.$$
There exists an invertible $F$-linear change of the variables after which the coefficient $a$ is nonzero. For any such coordinates put $L=F[Z]/(aZ^2+bZ+c)$ and write $z$ for the class of $Z$ [def-weil-polynomial-ring, def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient]. Let $B\subset Q(A)$ be the integral closure of $A$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure], where $Q(A)$ inverts all non-zero-divisors (elements whose multiplication is injective). Then $B$ is finite as an $A$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module], and there is a compatible $R$-algebra isomorphism
$$B\otimes_A R\cong L[[t]],\qquad X\mapsto zt,\quad Y\mapsto t,$$
identifying the structural image of $R$ with $F+tL[[t]]$. Tensor products and power series use [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product, def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. Under these maps $\mathfrak m^nR=t^nL[[t]]$ for every $n\ge1$. Completion induces residue-preserving ring isomorphisms $A/\mathfrak m^n\cong R/\mathfrak m^nR$ for every $n\ge1$ and a graded $F$-algebra isomorphism
$$\operatorname{gr}_{\mathfrak m}A\cong H:=F\oplus\bigoplus_{n\ge1}Lt^n\subset L[t]$$
[def-weil-pbc-associated-graded-ring]. If $d\in\mathfrak m^n$, its degree-$n$ initial class corresponds to the coefficient of $t^n$ in its image in $L[[t]]$, times $t^n$. In particular some $f\in\mathfrak m$ has initial class $t$ and image $t(1+th)$ with $h\in L[[t]]$. The normalization comparison extends the original map on fractions of $A$: every denominator is carried to the same denominator.

proof.text:
Choose a vector on which $q$ is nonzero: use $(1,0)$ if $a
e0$, $(0,1)$ if $a=0,c
e0$, and $(1,1)$ otherwise, since then $b
e0$. Complete it to a basis of $F^2$. The resulting substitution is invertible on power series coefficient by coefficient in each total degree, with inverse induced by the inverse matrix. Its new $X^2$ coefficient is nonzero. The discriminant changes by the square of the nonzero matrix determinant, as direct expansion shows, so it remains nonzero. Fix any coordinates with $a

source.place: Tag 0CBT (remark-quadratic-extension), construction (1): choice of a nonzero leading coefficient.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-curve-normalization-completion] to $A$: the hypotheses are precisely reduced, local, essentially of finite type over $k$, and dimension one. It gives finiteness of $B$ and identifies $B\otimes_A R$ with the integral closure of $R$ in $Q(R)$, by the map extending fractions with the same denominators. Apply [lem-sfb-quadratic-series-integral-closure] to the given presentation of $R$, using $a\ne0$ and the nonzero discriminant. Its map $X\mapsto zt$, $Y\mapsto t$ identifies that integral closure with $C=L[[t]]$ and the image of $R$ with $S=F+tC$. Composing these two identifications gives the required compatible $R$-algebra isomorphism. The first map supplies the stated fraction convention; the second fixes its restriction to $R$.

source.place: Tag 0C4A (lemma-2-branches-delta-1), proof, completion reduction and Cases I/II; varieties.tex Tag 0C3V (lemma-normalization-same-after-completion).

proof.text: Noetherianness means every ideal, in particular $\mathfrak m$, is finitely generated. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-mod-power] with $I=\mathfrak m$. For every $n\ge1$ it gives the quotient isomorphism $A/\mathfrak m^n\cong R/\mathfrak m^nR$, induced by the original completion map. These maps commute with the quotient transitions: both send the class of $a\in A$ to its completion class. At $n=1$ the kernel of $R\to F$ is therefore $\mathfrak mR$. The presentation and the substitution are residue-preserving, so in $S=F+tC$ this kernel is exactly $tC$.

source.place: Tag 05GG (lemma-hathat-finitely-generated), part (2), and the given residue-preserving presentation.

proof.text: In $S=F+tC$ we have $(tC)^n=t^nC$ for all $n\ge1$: a product of $n$ elements of $tC$ lies in $t^nC$, and conversely $t^nh$ is the product of $n-1$ copies of $t$ with $th$, all in $tC$. For $n=1$ the latter is just $th$. Extension of an ideal commutes with its products by expanding the finite sums of products defining them. Thus the equality $\mathfrak mR=tC$ from step 3 gives $\mathfrak m^nR=t^nC$ as subsets of $C$, not merely equality after extending the ideals to $C$.

source.place: Tag 0CBT (remark-quadratic-extension), omitted graded comparison: ideal-power calculation in the explicit image ring.

proof.text: For $n\ge1$, compare the kernels of the transition maps from exponent $n+1$ to exponent $n$ in step 3. They are respectively $\mathfrak m^n/\mathfrak m^{n+1}$ and $\mathfrak m^nR/\mathfrak m^{n+1}R$, so completion induces a bijection between these kernels. Degree zero is $A/\mathfrak m=F$. Using step 4, the positive-degree map is then $t^nC/t^{n+1}C\to Lt^n$, sending a series class to its coefficient of $t^n$ times $t^n$. This is a bijection: its kernel is exactly $t^{n+1}C$ and $\lambda t^n$ represents every $\lambda\in L$. Take the direct sum of these maps and the identity on degree zero. For series of orders at least $n,m$, the coefficient of degree $n+m$ of their product is the product of their coefficients of degrees $n,m$; terms of smaller degree vanish. Degree-zero multiplication is residue multiplication. The multiplication and scalar-action formulas of [def-weil-pbc-associated-graded-ring] therefore make this direct-sum bijection a graded $F$-algebra isomorphism onto $H$. This also proves the asserted formula for every initial class.

source.place: Tag 0CBT (remark-quadratic-extension), construction (3), explicit coefficient proof of the omitted associated-graded comparison; algebra.tex Tag 05GG for the already established quotient maps.

proof.text: The degree-one bijection of step 5 has $t\in Lt$ in its image. Choose a representative $f\in\mathfrak m$ of its inverse class. Its image in $C$ has zero constant term and coefficient $1$ at $t$, hence is $t+t^2h=t(1+th)$ for the series $h\in C$ obtained by shifting all higher coefficients down by two. This is exactly the required lift and its required expansion.

source.place: Tag 0CBT (remark-quadratic-extension), construction (3), degree-one lifting through the quotient map.

Step 1: if a=c=0 then b≠0, so one of (1,0),(0,1),(1,1) has nonzero q-value even in characteristic 2; the discriminant scales by det², and the coordinate change keeps the presentation continuous and residue-preserving. Step 2 relies only on the statements of the cited nodes. lem-trf-curve-normalization-completion has exactly this item's hypotheses (reduced, local, essentially finite type, dimension 1) and gives finiteness of B, B⊗Â equal to the integral closure, and the convention that denominators are kept. lem-sfb-quadratic-series-integral-closure (a≠0, disc≠0) gives j into L[[t]] with image F+tL[[t]]; transporting along the presentation and composing gives the R-algebra isomorphism. Step 3: the Mathlib leaf for 05GG with I=m (finitely generated by Noetherianity) gives A/mⁿ≅R/mⁿR; residue preservation together with j preserving constant terms gives mR=tC. Steps 4–6 are correctly elementary. (tC)ⁿ=tⁿC holds because tⁿh=t^{n-1}(th). The transition kernels compare with the tⁿ-coefficient map onto Ltⁿ, multiplication goes by lowest-order coefficients, and the F-action goes through A/m. The lift is f=t+t²h. These steps supply the graded comparison that Stacks 0CBT omits ('We omit the equivalence of this with (3)'); I read 0CBT, 0C4A (completion reduction, Cases I/II) and 0C3V in literature/stacks-project.
